claim: Letterman writes that before daylight on the morning of the 4th all the wounded within the lines, about twelve thousand on the two days, were removed to the hospitals.

source.edition: Medical Recollections of the Army of the Potomac, New York: D. Appleton and Company, 1866 (title page read)

quote: The Ambulance Corps performed its duty well. Before daylight on the morning of the 4th all the wounded within our lines (numbering on these two days about twelve thousand) were removed to the hospitals.

data.relation: removed the wounded within the lines to the hospitals before daylight on the 4th

value.unit: wounded within the lines on the two days (about)

date_scope.note: before daylight on the morning of the 4th

scene.may_show: Ambulances and bearers carrying the wounded from within the lines to the hospitals, the work finished before daylight on 4 July.

notes: the report of 3 October 1863 counts 14,193 wounded in all three days, including those of the first day who fell into enemy hands: a different population (see med.gettysburg-statistics.001)

claim: Letterman reports that, of 14,193 wounded, not one was left on the field within the lines early on the morning of July 4, and that a few found after daylight beyond the farthest pickets were brought in although the ambulance men were fired upon.

source.part: OR27-1-R016 Report of Surg. Jonathan Letterman, Medical Director, Army of the Potomac, 3 October 1863, on the medical department at the battle of Gettysburg

quote: Notwithstanding the great number of wounded, amounting to 14,193 ... not one wounded man of all that number was left on the field within our lines early on the morning of July 4. A few were found after daylight beyond our farthest pickets, and these were brought in, although the ambulance men were fired upon when engaged in this duty by the enemy

data.relation: cleared the field within the lines by early July 4; brought in a few found beyond the pickets under fire

scene.may_show: Ambulance men bringing in the few wounded found beyond the farthest pickets after daylight on 4 July, fired upon by the enemy.
